title: Two-Game and Five-Game Weeks: Lineup and Streaming Adjustments
brief: How should we adjust daily lineups, streaming adds (max 6 per week) and percentage-category expectations in weeks when a team plays only 2 or as many as 5 games? It must cover why low-volume weeks make FG% and FT% swing, why back-to-back counts matter little except for players returning from injury, and how merged NBA Cup weeks change the count.
summary: Games played matter most in head-to-head, so use all 6 weekly adds to cover your short weeks. Target streamers who play on days with fewer than 10 or 11 NBA games, and count the merged NBA Cup matchup as one 14-day block. Treat FG% and FT% as coin flips when your volume is low. Ignore back-to-back counts, except for players just back from injury. The schedule factor that really matters is a two-game week in our playoffs (weeks 19 to 21, ending 2027-03-28).

sections.heading: Why short weeks make FG% and FT% swing

paragraphs.text: FG% and FT% are team ratios. In a week when your roster plays few games, you take fewer shots, so each miss moves the percentage more. Results swing more, and percentage categories are not safe. FG% varies most from game to game and week to week. FT% varies most from year to year.

Shooting categories have no floor. A bad shooter keeps dragging you down for as long as he plays. You can lose a lead in FG% or FT% on the last day of a matchup. In a low-volume week, do not count a percentage category as won on Friday. Check the totals every day through Sunday.

Low volume also comes from roster construction. A heavy punt cuts your volume and adds variance. Combine a punt build with a short schedule week and expect the percentage results to be close to random.

There is one upside. Missing games from injuries or a thin schedule cuts your turnovers on its own. So in a week when you are short on games, you will often win TO anyway. The reverse is also true. Streaming for games raises turnovers, so chasing low TO works against the head-to-head games-played edge.

sections.heading: Daily lineups and the 6 weekly adds

paragraphs.text: Use every add you have. With a weekly limit, the notes say to use all your pickups. In our league that means all 6, every week. The waiver wire matters as much as the draft. Streaming for a games-played edge wins head-to-head weeks.

Your last roster spots should churn. Streaming players ranked about 170 to 190 for extra games beats holding a player ranked about 130 who sits on your bench. Only 144 players get drafted here. So the players you stream will mostly come from just below the draft pool.

Pick streamers by day, not just by weekly total. A quality game is one played on a day with few NBA games, so you face no start/sit decision. Set the cutoff at 10 or 11 games on a day, not Basketball Monster's default of 5. On a busy day, an extra streamer may just sit on your bench. On a light day, he fills a G, F, C or Util slot that would be empty otherwise.

In a week when one of your regulars plays only 2 games, he leaves empty slots on the other days. Even good per-game numbers can lose you the week if he plays about two games. Fill the gaps with streamers whose games fall on those open days. In a week when a player plays 5 games, keep him active every day he plays. His extra attempts also make your FG% and FT% more stable.

Best streaming targets: backup centers who start when the starter sits, and bench players on thin teams during heavy schedule stretches when starters rest. Also note teams on a long travel run with no back-to-back home or road games. That stretch can wear a team down.

sections.heading: Back-to-backs: ignore them unless a player is returning from injury

paragraphs.text: Team back-to-back totals only range from 13 to 16. Over a 25-week season, the best and worst teams differ by about three back-to-backs. That is about one game every two months. Several experts agree it should not move draft prices or weekly lineup decisions.

The exception is players coming back from in-season injuries. They may sit one night of a back-to-back. Most back-to-back problems come from these players, and nobody can predict them in October. For a recently returned player, check the injury report before counting his games for the week. If his week has a back-to-back, plan for one game fewer than the schedule shows.

sections.heading: Merged NBA Cup and All-Star weeks

paragraphs.text: Treat the two NBA Cup half weeks (November 30 to December 13) as one 14-day matchup. Treat the All-Star weeks the same way. One note says Yahoo combines weeks seven and eight into one matchup for the NBA Cup this season. Confirm in our league's schedule page that the Cup weeks are merged.

In a merged matchup, count games over the full 14 days, not per half week. A team with a 2-game half might be fine once both halves are added. Higher volume over two weeks also steadies FG% and FT% compared with a single short week. Check whether the 6-add limit applies per calendar week or per matchup inside the merged block. Then plan your streaming adds across both halves.

sections.heading: Draft day, week one and the playoffs

paragraphs.text: At the 2026-10-18 auction, do not pay for schedules. Quality game totals vary too little between teams to affect draft decisions. Do not spend late dollars on a player because his week one schedule is good. Use the first two weeks to judge players, and accept a loss in week one or two to keep fliers with long-term value.

The experts lean different ways on early streaming. One view: stream all season for a games-played edge, and use all your adds. The other view: do not stream just to get extra games in the opening weeks. Keep those roster spots for fliers who may break out. A fair middle path for us: in weeks one and two, use adds only on open spots, not on cutting fliers. After that, use all 6 every week.

Two-game weeks in the fantasy playoffs are the schedule factor that actually matters. In head-to-head, a two-game playoff week should drop a player down your board. Use the schedule that ends on March 28 for weeks 19, 20 and 21. Before the 2027-03-04 trade deadline, count each starter's games in those three weeks. Trade away players with two-game playoff weeks for players with fuller weeks. During the playoffs themselves, smart streaming keeps you ahead on games.
